v: Since many have undertaken to compile an account of the events that have been fulfilled[^1] among us,
Ἐπειδήπερ πολλοὶ ἐπεχείρησαν ἀνατάξασθαι διήγησιν περὶ τῶν πεπληροφορημένων ἐν ἡμῖν πραγμάτων,
just as they were handed down to us by those who were eyewitnesses from the beginning and became servants of the word,[^2]
καθὼς παρέδοσαν ἡμῖν οἱ ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς αὐτόπται καὶ ὑπηρέται γενόμενοι τοῦ λόγου,
it seemed good to me as well, having carefully investigated everything from the start,[^3] to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus,[^4]
ἔδοξε κἀμοὶ παρηκολουθηκότι ἄνωθεν πᾶσιν ἀκριβῶς καθεξῆς σοι γράψαι, κράτιστε Θεόφιλε,
so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught.[^5]
ἵνα ἐπιγνῷς περὶ ὧν κατηχήθης λόγων τὴν ἀσφάλειαν.
In the days of Herod king of Judea,[^6] there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah.[^7] His wife was a descendant of Aaron,[^8] and her name was Elizabeth.
Ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἡρῴδου βασιλέως τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἱερεύς τις ὀνόματι Ζαχαρίας ἐξ ἐφημερίας Ἀβιά, καὶ γυνὴ αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν θυγατέρων Ἀαρών, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆς Ἐλισάβετ.
Both of them were righteous in the sight of God, living blamelessly by all the commandments and decrees of the Lord.[^9]
ἦσαν δὲ δίκαιοι ἀμφότεροι ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ, πορευόμενοι ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐντολαῖς καὶ δικαιώμασιν τοῦ κυρίου ἄμεμπτοι.
But they had no child, because Elizabeth was unable to have children, and both of them were well along in years.[^10]
καὶ οὐκ ἦν αὐτοῖς τέκνον, καθότι ἦν ἡ Ἐλισάβετ στεῖρα, καὶ ἀμφότεροι προβεβηκότες ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτῶν ἦσαν.
Once, when Zechariah was serving as priest before God while his division was on duty,
Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἱερατεύειν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ τάξει τῆς ἐφημερίας αὐτοῦ ἔναντι τοῦ θεοῦ
he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to go into the sanctuary[^11] of the Lord and burn incense.
κατὰ τὸ ἔθος τῆς ἱερατείας ἔλαχε τοῦ θυμιᾶσαι εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ κυρίου,
At the hour of the incense offering, the whole crowd of people was praying outside.
καὶ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος ἦν τοῦ λαοῦ προσευχόμενον ἔξω τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ θυμιάματος·
Then an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.
ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἑστὼς ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ θυμιάματος.
When Zechariah saw him, he was shaken, and fear came over him.
καὶ ἐταράχθη Ζαχαρίας ἰδών, καὶ φόβος ἐπέπεσεν ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
But the angel said to him, "Don't be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to name him John.
εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ ἄγγελος· Μὴ φοβοῦ, Ζαχαρία, διότι εἰσηκούσθη ἡ δέησίς σου, καὶ ἡ γυνή σου Ἐλισάβετ γεννήσει υἱόν σοι, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰωάννην·
You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth,
καὶ ἔσται χαρά σοι καὶ ἀγαλλίασις, καὶ πολλοὶ ἐπὶ τῇ γενέσει αὐτοῦ χαρήσονται·
for he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He must never drink wine or strong drink,[^12] and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even before he is born.[^13]
ἔσται γὰρ μέγας ἐνώπιον τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ οἶνον καὶ σίκερα οὐ μὴ πίῃ, καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου πλησθήσεται ἔτι ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ,
He will turn many of the people of Israel back to the Lord their God.
καὶ πολλοὺς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐπιστρέψει ἐπὶ κύριον τὸν θεὸν αὐτῶν·

And he will go ahead of him[^14] in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers to their children[^15] and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to make ready for the Lord a people prepared."
καὶ αὐτὸς προελεύσεται ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ἐν πνεύματι καὶ δυνάμει Ἠλίου, ἐπιστρέψαι καρδίας πατέρων ἐπὶ τέκνα καὶ ἀπειθεῖς ἐν φρονήσει δικαίων, ἑτοιμάσαι κυρίῳ λαὸν κατεσκευασμένον.
Zechariah said to the angel, "How can I be sure of this?[^16] I am an old man, and my wife is well along in years."
καὶ εἶπεν Ζαχαρίας πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον· Κατὰ τί γνώσομαι τοῦτο; ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι πρεσβύτης καὶ ἡ γυνή μου προβεβηκυῖα ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτῆς.
The angel answered him, "I am Gabriel.[^17] I stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Γαβριὴλ ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἀπεστάλην λαλῆσαι πρὸς σὲ καὶ εὐαγγελίσασθαί σοι ταῦτα·
Look, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their proper time."
καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔσῃ σιωπῶν καὶ μὴ δυνάμενος λαλῆσαι ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας γένηται ταῦτα, ἀνθʼ ὧν οὐκ ἐπίστευσας τοῖς λόγοις μου, οἵτινες πληρωθήσονται εἰς τὸν καιρὸν αὐτῶν.
Meanwhile the people were waiting for Zechariah, and they wondered why he was staying so long in the sanctuary.
Καὶ ἦν ὁ λαὸς προσδοκῶν τὸν Ζαχαρίαν, καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ἐν τῷ χρονίζειν ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτόν.
When he came out, he could not speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the sanctuary. He kept making signs to them, and he remained mute.[^18]
ἐξελθὼν δὲ οὐκ ἐδύνατο λαλῆσαι αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν ὅτι ὀπτασίαν ἑώρακεν ἐν τῷ ναῷ· καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διανεύων αὐτοῖς, καὶ διέμενεν κωφός.
When his days of service were completed, he went back to his home.
καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τῆς λειτουργίας αὐτοῦ, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
After those days his wife Elizabeth became pregnant, and for five months she kept herself in seclusion. She said,
Μετὰ δὲ ταύτας τὰς ἡμέρας συνέλαβεν Ἐλισάβετ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ· καὶ περιέκρυβεν ἑαυτὴν μῆνας πέντε, λέγουσα
"This is what the Lord has done for me in these days, when he looked on me to take away my disgrace among people."
ὅτι Οὕτως μοι πεποίηκεν κύριος ἐν ἡμέραις αἷς ἐπεῖδεν ἀφελεῖν ὄνειδός μου ἐν ἀνθρώποις.
In the sixth month[^19] the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a town in Galilee called Nazareth,
Ἐν δὲ τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀπεστάλη ὁ ἄγγελος Γαβριὴλ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ᾗ ὄνομα Ναζαρὲθ
to a virgin engaged[^20] to a man named Joseph, of the house of David. The virgin's name was Mary.
πρὸς παρθένον ἐμνηστευμένην ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰωσὴφ ἐξ οἴκου Δαυίδ, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς παρθένου Μαριάμ.
The angel came to her and said, "Greetings, you who are highly favored![^21] The Lord is with you."[^22]
καὶ εἰσελθὼν πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπεν· Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ὁ κύριος μετὰ σοῦ.
She was greatly troubled by his words[^23] and wondered what kind of greeting this might be.
ἡ δὲ ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ διεταράχθη καὶ διελογίζετο ποταπὸς εἴη ὁ ἀσπασμὸς οὗτος.
The angel said to her, "Don't be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
καὶ εἶπεν ὁ ἄγγελος αὐτῇ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, Μαριάμ, εὗρες γὰρ χάριν παρὰ τῷ θεῷ·
Look, you will become pregnant and give birth to a son, and you are to name him Jesus.[^24]
καὶ ἰδοὺ συλλήμψῃ ἐν γαστρὶ καὶ τέξῃ υἱόν, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν.
He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his ancestor David,[^25]
οὗτος ἔσται μέγας καὶ υἱὸς Ὑψίστου κληθήσεται, καὶ δώσει αὐτῷ κύριος ὁ θεὸς τὸν θρόνον Δαυὶδ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ,
and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever. His kingdom will never end."
καὶ βασιλεύσει ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰακὼβ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, καὶ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔσται τέλος.
Mary said to the angel, "How will this be, since I have not been with a man?"[^26]
εἶπεν δὲ Μαριὰμ πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον· Πῶς ἔσται τοῦτο, ἐπεὶ ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω;
The angel answered her, "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God.[^27]
καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ δύναμις Ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι· διὸ καὶ τὸ γεννώμενον ἅγιον κληθήσεται, υἱὸς θεοῦ·
And look, your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age. She who was said to be unable to have children is now in her sixth month.
καὶ ἰδοὺ Ἐλισάβετ ἡ συγγενίς σου καὶ αὐτὴ συνείληφεν υἱὸν ἐν γήρει αὐτῆς, καὶ οὗτος μὴν ἕκτος ἐστὶν αὐτῇ τῇ καλουμένῃ στείρᾳ·
For no word from God will be without power."[^28]
ὅτι οὐκ ἀδυνατήσει παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ πᾶν ῥῆμα.
Mary said, "Here I am, the Lord's servant.[^29] Let it happen to me as you have said." Then the angel left her.
εἶπεν δὲ Μαριάμ· Ἰδοὺ ἡ δούλη κυρίου· γένοιτό μοι κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου. καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ἀπʼ αὐτῆς ὁ ἄγγελος.
In those days Mary got up and went with haste into the hill country, to a town of Judah.
Ἀναστᾶσα δὲ Μαριὰμ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἐπορεύθη εἰς τὴν ὀρεινὴν μετὰ σπουδῆς εἰς πόλιν Ἰούδα,
She went into Zechariah's house and greeted Elizabeth.
καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον Ζαχαρίου καὶ ἠσπάσατο τὴν Ἐλισάβετ.
When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤκουσεν τὸν ἀσπασμὸν τῆς Μαρίας ἡ Ἐλισάβετ, ἐσκίρτησεν τὸ βρέφος ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐπλήσθη πνεύματος ἁγίου ἡ Ἐλισάβετ,
She cried out with a loud shout, "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
καὶ ἀνεφώνησεν κραυγῇ μεγάλῃ καὶ εἶπεν· Εὐλογημένη σὺ ἐν γυναιξίν, καὶ εὐλογημένος ὁ καρπὸς τῆς κοιλίας σου.
Why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
καὶ πόθεν μοι τοῦτο ἵνα ἔλθῃ ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ κυρίου μου πρὸς ἐμέ;
For as soon as the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy.
ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὡς ἐγένετο ἡ φωνὴ τοῦ ἀσπασμοῦ σου εἰς τὰ ὦτά μου, ἐσκίρτησεν ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει τὸ βρέφος ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ μου.
Blessed[^30] is she who believed that what the Lord has said to her will be fulfilled."[^31]
καὶ μακαρία ἡ πιστεύσασα ὅτι ἔσται τελείωσις τοῖς λελαλημένοις αὐτῇ παρὰ κυρίου.
And Mary said: "My soul proclaims the greatness of the Lord,[^32]
Καὶ εἶπεν Μαριάμ· Μεγαλύνει ἡ ψυχή μου τὸν κύριον,
and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
καὶ ἠγαλλίασεν τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπὶ τῷ θεῷ τῷ σωτῆρί μου·
for he has looked with favor on the lowliness[^33] of his servant. Yes, from now on all generations will call me blessed,
ὅτι ἐπέβλεψεν ἐπὶ τὴν ταπείνωσιν τῆς δούλης αὐτοῦ, ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν μακαριοῦσίν με πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαί·
for the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.
ὅτι ἐποίησέν μοι μεγάλα ὁ δυνατός, καὶ ἅγιον τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ,
His mercy is from generation to generation for those who fear him.
καὶ τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ εἰς γενεὰς καὶ γενεὰς τοῖς φοβουμένοις αὐτόν.
He has done mighty deeds with his arm; he has scattered those who are proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
Ἐποίησεν κράτος ἐν βραχίονι αὐτοῦ, διεσκόρπισεν ὑπερηφάνους διανοίᾳ καρδίας αὐτῶν·
He has brought down rulers from their thrones and lifted up the lowly.
καθεῖλεν δυνάστας ἀπὸ θρόνων καὶ ὕψωσεν ταπεινούς,
He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.
πεινῶντας ἐνέπλησεν ἀγαθῶν καὶ πλουτοῦντας ἐξαπέστειλεν κενούς.
He has come to the help of his servant Israel, remembering his mercy,
ἀντελάβετο Ἰσραὴλ παιδὸς αὐτοῦ, μνησθῆναι ἐλέους,
as he promised our ancestors, to Abraham and his descendants forever."[^34]
καθὼς ἐλάλησεν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν, τῷ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
Mary stayed with Elizabeth about three months and then returned to her home.
Ἔμεινεν δὲ Μαριὰμ σὺν αὐτῇ ὡς μῆνας τρεῖς, καὶ ὑπέστρεψεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς.
When the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, she had a son.
Τῇ δὲ Ἐλισάβετ ἐπλήσθη ὁ χρόνος τοῦ τεκεῖν αὐτήν, καὶ ἐγέννησεν υἱόν.
Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown her his great mercy,[^35] and they rejoiced with her.
καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ περίοικοι καὶ οἱ συγγενεῖς αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐμεγάλυνεν κύριος τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτῆς, καὶ συνέχαιρον αὐτῇ.
On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were going to name him Zechariah, after his father.
Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἦλθον περιτεμεῖν τὸ παιδίον, καὶ ἐκάλουν αὐτὸ ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ Ζαχαρίαν.
But his mother answered, "No! He is to be called John."
καὶ ἀποκριθεῖσα ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Οὐχί, ἀλλὰ κληθήσεται Ἰωάννης.
They said to her, "None of your relatives has that name."
καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτὴν ὅτι Οὐδείς ἐστιν ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου ὃς καλεῖται τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ.
Then they made signs to his father to find out what he wanted him to be called.
ἐνένευον δὲ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ τὸ τί ἂν θέλοι καλεῖσθαι αὐτό.
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, "His name is John." And they were all amazed.
καὶ αἰτήσας πινακίδιον ἔγραψεν λέγων· Ἰωάννης ἐστὶν ὄνομα αὐτοῦ. καὶ ἐθαύμασαν πάντες.
Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue set free,[^36] and he began to speak, praising God.
ἀνεῴχθη δὲ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ παραχρῆμα καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐλάλει εὐλογῶν τὸν θεόν.
Fear came over all their neighbors, and throughout the hill country of Judea people talked about all these things.
καὶ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ πάντας φόβος τοὺς περιοικοῦντας αὐτούς, καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ὀρεινῇ τῆς Ἰουδαίας διελαλεῖτο πάντα τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα,
All who heard of them kept them in mind,[^37] asking, "What then will this child become?" For the hand of the Lord was with him.
καὶ ἔθεντο πάντες οἱ ἀκούσαντες ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῶν, λέγοντες· Τί ἄρα τὸ παιδίον τοῦτο ἔσται; καὶ γὰρ χεὶρ κυρίου ἦν μετʼ αὐτοῦ.
His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied:
Καὶ Ζαχαρίας ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐπλήσθη πνεύματος ἁγίου καὶ ἐπροφήτευσεν λέγων·
"Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel,[^38] because he has come to help[^39] his people and has brought them redemption.
Εὐλογητὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, ὅτι ἐπεσκέψατο καὶ ἐποίησεν λύτρωσιν τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ,
He has raised up a horn of salvation[^40] for us in the house of his servant David,
καὶ ἤγειρεν κέρας σωτηρίας ἡμῖν ἐν οἴκῳ Δαυὶδ παιδὸς αὐτοῦ,
as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets long ago:
καθὼς ἐλάλησεν διὰ στόματος τῶν ἁγίων ἀπʼ αἰῶνος προφητῶν αὐτοῦ,
salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,
σωτηρίαν ἐξ ἐχθρῶν ἡμῶν καὶ ἐκ χειρὸς πάντων τῶν μισούντων ἡμᾶς,
to show mercy to our ancestors and to remember his holy covenant,
ποιῆσαι ἔλεος μετὰ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν καὶ μνησθῆναι διαθήκης ἁγίας αὐτοῦ,
the oath he swore to our father Abraham, to grant us
ὅρκον ὃν ὤμοσεν πρὸς Ἀβραὰμ τὸν πατέρα ἡμῶν, τοῦ δοῦναι ἡμῖν
that, rescued from the hand of enemies, we might serve him without fear
ἀφόβως ἐκ χειρὸς ἐχθρῶν ῥυσθέντας λατρεύειν αὐτῷ
in holiness and righteousness before him all our days.
ἐν ὁσιότητι καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ πάσαις ταῖς ἡμέραις ἡμῶν.
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways,[^41]
καὶ σὺ δέ, παιδίον, προφήτης Ὑψίστου κληθήσῃ, προπορεύσῃ γὰρ ἐνώπιον κυρίου ἑτοιμάσαι ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ,
to give his people the knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins,
τοῦ δοῦναι γνῶσιν σωτηρίας τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀφέσει ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν,
because of the tender mercy[^42] of our God, by which the dawn[^43] from on high will come to us,[^44]
διὰ σπλάγχνα ἐλέους θεοῦ ἡμῶν, ἐν οἷς ἐπισκέψεται ἡμᾶς ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους,
to shine on those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death,[^45] to guide our feet into the way of peace."
ἐπιφᾶναι τοῖς ἐν σκότει καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου καθημένοις, τοῦ κατευθῦναι τοὺς πόδας ἡμῶν εἰς ὁδὸν εἰρήνης.
The child grew and became strong in spirit.[^46] He lived in the wilderness until the day he appeared publicly to Israel.
Τὸ δὲ παιδίον ηὔξανε καὶ ἐκραταιοῦτο πνεύματι, καὶ ἦν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις ἕως ἡμέρας ἀναδείξεως αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸν Ἰσραήλ.

n.1: Or "fully established". Verses 1–4 are a single sentence in Greek, written in the formal style that Greek historians used to open their works.
n.2: That is, the message. Greek *logos*, "word, message".
n.3: Or "having followed everything closely for a long time". Greek *anothen* can mean "from the beginning" or "for a long time".
n.4: *Most excellent* is a respectful title for people of high rank, used of Roman governors in Acts 23:26; 24:3; 26:25. *Theophilus* means "friend of God" or "loved by God".
n.5: Or "informed about".
n.6: Herod the Great, who ruled Judea as king under Rome from 37 to 4 BC.
n.7: The priests were divided into twenty-four divisions, which took turns serving in the temple. Abijah was the eighth (1 Chronicles 24:10).
n.8: Literally "from the daughters of Aaron", that is, from a priestly family.
n.9: Greek *kyrios*. In Luke 1–2, as in the Greek Old Testament, "the Lord" usually means God, standing for the divine name Yahweh.
n.10: Literally "advanced in their days"; also in verse 18.
n.11: Greek *naos*, the sanctuary building itself, as distinct from the temple courts where the people stood (verse 10); also in verses 21–22.
n.12: Compare Numbers 6:3; Judges 13:4.
n.13: Literally "even from his mother's womb".
n.14: That is, ahead of the Lord their God (verse 16).
n.16: Literally "By what will I know this?"
n.18: Greek *kophos*, which can mean unable to speak, unable to hear, or both (compare verse 62).
n.20: Or "betrothed". A Jewish engagement was a binding agreement that could be ended only by divorce, but the couple did not yet live together.
n.21: *Greetings*: Greek *chaire*, the usual greeting, literally "Rejoice!" *Highly favored*: or "graced", from *charis*, "grace, favor".
n.22: Many manuscripts add "Blessed are you among women."
n.23: Many manuscripts read "When she saw him, she was greatly troubled at his words".
n.24: Greek *Iesous*, the Greek form of the Hebrew name Joshua, which means "Yahweh saves".
n.26: Literally "since I do not know a man", a Hebrew way of speaking of sexual relations.
n.27: Or "So the holy child to be born will be called the Son of God."
n.28: Or "For nothing will be impossible with God." Greek *rhema* means "word" or "thing". Many manuscripts read "with God" for "from God", giving "For with God nothing will be impossible." Compare Genesis 18:14.
n.29: Or "slave". Greek *doule*, a female servant or slave; also in verse 48.
n.30: Greek *makaria*, "happy, fortunate", a different word from "blessed" in verse 42.
n.31: Or "Blessed is she who believed, for what the Lord has said to her will be fulfilled."
n.32: Traditionally "magnifies the Lord". The song (verses 46–55) is known as the Magnificat, from its first word in Latin. It has many echoes of Hannah's song in 1 Samuel 2:1–10.
n.34: Literally "as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever". The words "to Abraham" may also go with "remembering his mercy" in verse 54: "remembering his mercy to Abraham and his descendants forever, as he promised our ancestors."
n.35: Literally "had magnified his mercy with her".
n.36: The Greek has no verb for the tongue: literally "his mouth was opened, and his tongue".
n.37: Literally "laid them up in their heart".
n.38: Compare Psalm 41:14 (41:13 in most English Bibles); 72:18; 106:48. In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, Yahweh. Zechariah's song (verses 68–79) is known as the Benedictus, from its first word in Latin.
n.39: Literally "visited", in the sense of coming to look after (Genesis 50:24; Exodus 4:31); also in verse 78.
n.40: The horn is a picture of strength: a mighty savior. Compare Psalm 18:3 (18:2 in most English Bibles); 132:17.
n.42: Literally "the inward parts of mercy", the inner organs being thought of as the seat of feelings.
n.43: Greek *anatole*, "rising", used of the sunrise and of a rising star. In the Greek Old Testament it also translates "Branch", a title for the coming king (Jeremiah 23:5; Zechariah 3:8; 6:12).
n.44: Many manuscripts read "has come to us".
n.45: Compare Isaiah 9:1 (9:2 in most English Bibles); Psalm 107:10. "Shadow of death" is the Greek Old Testament's rendering of the Hebrew word translated "deep darkness" in those verses.

v: In those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus[^1] that the whole world[^2] should be registered.
Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἐξῆλθεν δόγμα παρὰ Καίσαρος Αὐγούστου ἀπογράφεσθαι πᾶσαν τὴν οἰκουμένην·
(This was the first registration, made while Quirinius was governor of Syria.)[^3]
(αὕτη ἀπογραφὴ πρώτη ἐγένετο ἡγεμονεύοντος τῆς Συρίας Κυρηνίου·)
Everyone went to be registered, each to his own town.
καὶ ἐπορεύοντο πάντες ἀπογράφεσθαι, ἕκαστος εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ πόλιν.
Joseph also went up from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to the town of David called Bethlehem,[^4] because he was of the house and family line of David.
Ἀνέβη δὲ καὶ Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἐκ πόλεως Ναζαρὲθ εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν εἰς πόλιν Δαυὶδ ἥτις καλεῖται Βηθλέεμ, διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐξ οἴκου καὶ πατριᾶς Δαυίδ,
He went to be registered with Mary, who was engaged to him[^5] and was expecting a child.
ἀπογράψασθαι σὺν Μαριὰμ τῇ ἐμνηστευμένῃ αὐτῷ, οὔσῃ ἐγκύῳ.
While they were there, the time came for her to give birth,
ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἐκεῖ ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ τεκεῖν αὐτήν,
and she gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in strips of cloth[^6] and laid him in a manger,[^7] because there was no room for them in the guest room.[^8]
καὶ ἔτεκεν τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς τὸν πρωτότοκον, καὶ ἐσπαργάνωσεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἀνέκλινεν αὐτὸν ἐν φάτνῃ, διότι οὐκ ἦν αὐτοῖς τόπος ἐν τῷ καταλύματι.
In the same region there were shepherds living out in the fields, keeping watch over their flock at night.
Καὶ ποιμένες ἦσαν ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ τῇ αὐτῇ ἀγραυλοῦντες καὶ φυλάσσοντες φυλακὰς τῆς νυκτὸς ἐπὶ τὴν ποίμνην αὐτῶν.
An angel of the Lord stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.[^9]
καὶ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἐπέστη αὐτοῖς καὶ δόξα κυρίου περιέλαμψεν αὐτούς, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν φόβον μέγαν·
But the angel said to them, "Don't be afraid. Look, I am bringing you good news of great joy, which will be for all the people.
καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ ἄγγελος· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε, ἰδοὺ γὰρ εὐαγγελίζομαι ὑμῖν χαρὰν μεγάλην ἥτις ἔσται παντὶ τῷ λαῷ,
Today in the town of David a Savior has been born for you. He is the Messiah, the Lord.[^10]
ὅτι ἐτέχθη ὑμῖν σήμερον σωτὴρ ὅς ἐστιν χριστὸς κύριος ἐν πόλει Δαυίδ·
This will be the sign for you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth and lying in a manger."
καὶ τοῦτο ὑμῖν τὸ σημεῖον, εὑρήσετε βρέφος ἐσπαργανωμένον καὶ κείμενον ἐν φάτνῃ.
Suddenly a great company of the heavenly army[^11] appeared with the angel, praising God and saying,
καὶ ἐξαίφνης ἐγένετο σὺν τῷ ἀγγέλῳ πλῆθος στρατιᾶς οὐρανίου αἰνούντων τὸν θεὸν καὶ λεγόντων·
"Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace among people with whom he is pleased!"[^12]
Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις θεῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς εἰρήνη ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκίας.
When the angels had left them and gone back into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, "Let us go over to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us."
Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἀπῆλθον ἀπʼ αὐτῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν οἱ ἄγγελοι, οἱ ποιμένες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Διέλθωμεν δὴ ἕως Βηθλέεμ καὶ ἴδωμεν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο τὸ γεγονὸς ὃ ὁ κύριος ἐγνώρισεν ἡμῖν.
So they hurried off and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger.
καὶ ἦλθαν σπεύσαντες καὶ ἀνεῦραν τήν τε Μαριὰμ καὶ τὸν Ἰωσὴφ καὶ τὸ βρέφος κείμενον ἐν τῇ φάτνῃ·
When they had seen him, they made known what they had been told about this child.
ἰδόντες δὲ ἐγνώρισαν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος τοῦ λαληθέντος αὐτοῖς περὶ τοῦ παιδίου τούτου.
All who heard it were amazed at what the shepherds told them.
καὶ πάντες οἱ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν περὶ τῶν λαληθέντων ὑπὸ τῶν ποιμένων πρὸς αὐτούς,
But Mary treasured up all these things, pondering them in her heart.
ἡ δὲ Μαρία πάντα συνετήρει τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα συμβάλλουσα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς.
The shepherds went back, glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen, just as they had been told.
καὶ ὑπέστρεψαν οἱ ποιμένες δοξάζοντες καὶ αἰνοῦντες τὸν θεὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἤκουσαν καὶ εἶδον καθὼς ἐλαλήθη πρὸς αὐτούς.
When eight days had passed and it was time to circumcise him, he was named Jesus, the name the angel had given him before he was conceived in the womb.
Καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ τοῦ περιτεμεῖν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐκλήθη τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦς, τὸ κληθὲν ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγγέλου πρὸ τοῦ συλλημφθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ.
When the days of their purification[^13] according to the Law of Moses were completed, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord
Καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸν νόμον Μωϋσέως, ἀνήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παραστῆσαι τῷ κυρίῳ,
(as it is written in the Law of the Lord, "Every male who first opens the womb will be called holy to the Lord"),[^14]
καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν νόμῳ κυρίου ὅτι Πᾶν ἄρσεν διανοῖγον μήτραν ἅγιον τῷ κυρίῳ κληθήσεται,
and to offer a sacrifice according to what is said in the Law of the Lord: "a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons."[^15]
καὶ τοῦ δοῦναι θυσίαν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν τῷ νόμῳ κυρίου, ζεῦγος τρυγόνων ἢ δύο νοσσοὺς περιστερῶν.
Now there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, and he was waiting for the comfort of Israel.[^16] The Holy Spirit was on him,
Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος ἦν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ ᾧ ὄνομα Συμεών, καὶ ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος καὶ εὐλαβής, προσδεχόμενος παράκλησιν τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, καὶ πνεῦμα ἦν ἅγιον ἐπʼ αὐτόν·
and it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Messiah.[^17]
καὶ ἦν αὐτῷ κεχρηματισμένον ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον πρὶν ἢ ἂν ἴδῃ τὸν χριστὸν κυρίου.
Led by the Spirit,[^18] he came into the temple. When the parents brought in the child Jesus to do for him what the Law required,
καὶ ἦλθεν ἐν τῷ πνεύματι εἰς τὸ ἱερόν· καὶ ἐν τῷ εἰσαγαγεῖν τοὺς γονεῖς τὸ παιδίον Ἰησοῦν τοῦ ποιῆσαι αὐτοὺς κατὰ τὸ εἰθισμένον τοῦ νόμου περὶ αὐτοῦ
Simeon took him in his arms, praised God, and said:
καὶ αὐτὸς ἐδέξατο αὐτὸ εἰς τὰς ἀγκάλας καὶ εὐλόγησεν τὸν θεὸν καὶ εἶπεν·
"Now, Master, you are letting your servant go[^19] in peace, as you promised,[^20]
Νῦν ἀπολύεις τὸν δοῦλόν σου, δέσποτα, κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου ἐν εἰρήνῃ·
for my eyes have seen your salvation,
ὅτι εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου τὸ σωτήριόν σου
which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples:
ὃ ἡτοίμασας κατὰ πρόσωπον πάντων τῶν λαῶν,
a light for revelation to the Gentiles,[^21] and glory for your people Israel."
φῶς εἰς ἀποκάλυψιν ἐθνῶν καὶ δόξαν λαοῦ σου Ἰσραήλ.
The child's father and mother were amazed at what was being said about him.[^22]
καὶ ἦν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ θαυμάζοντες ἐπὶ τοῖς λαλουμένοις περὶ αὐτοῦ.
Then Simeon blessed them and said to his mother Mary, "Look, this child is destined to cause the falling and rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed,[^23]
καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς Συμεὼν καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς Μαριὰμ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ· Ἰδοὺ οὗτος κεῖται εἰς πτῶσιν καὶ ἀνάστασιν πολλῶν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ εἰς σημεῖον ἀντιλεγόμενον,
and a sword will pierce your own soul too, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed."
καὶ σοῦ δὲ αὐτῆς τὴν ψυχὴν διελεύσεται ῥομφαία, ὅπως ἂν ἀποκαλυφθῶσιν ἐκ πολλῶν καρδιῶν διαλογισμοί.
There was also a prophet, Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was very old. After her marriage[^24] she had lived with her husband seven years,
Καὶ ἦν Ἅννα προφῆτις, θυγάτηρ Φανουήλ, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἀσήρ (αὕτη προβεβηκυῖα ἐν ἡμέραις πολλαῖς, ζήσασα μετὰ ἀνδρὸς ἔτη ἑπτὰ ἀπὸ τῆς παρθενίας αὐτῆς,
and then she had been a widow until she was eighty-four.[^25] She never left the temple, but worshiped night and day with fasting and prayer.
καὶ αὐτὴ χήρα ἕως ἐτῶν ὀγδοήκοντα τεσσάρων,) ἣ οὐκ ἀφίστατο τοῦ ἱεροῦ νηστείαις καὶ δεήσεσιν λατρεύουσα νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν.
At that very hour she came up and began to give thanks to God and to speak about the child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.[^26]
καὶ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐπιστᾶσα ἀνθωμολογεῖτο τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλάλει περὶ αὐτοῦ πᾶσιν τοῖς προσδεχομένοις λύτρωσιν Ἰερουσαλήμ.
When they had done everything the Law of the Lord required, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
Καὶ ὡς ἐτέλεσαν πάντα τὰ κατὰ τὸν νόμον κυρίου, ἐπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν εἰς πόλιν ἑαυτῶν Ναζαρέθ.
The child grew and became strong,[^27] filled with wisdom, and the favor[^28] of God was on him.
Τὸ δὲ παιδίον ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐκραταιοῦτο πληρούμενον σοφίᾳ, καὶ χάρις θεοῦ ἦν ἐπʼ αὐτό.
Every year his parents went to Jerusalem for the festival of the Passover.
Καὶ ἐπορεύοντο οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ κατʼ ἔτος εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ τῇ ἑορτῇ τοῦ πάσχα.
When he was twelve years old, they went up as usual for the festival.[^29]
καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἐτῶν δώδεκα, ἀναβαινόντων αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸ ἔθος τῆς ἑορτῆς
When the days of the festival were over, as they were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, but his parents did not know it.[^30]
καὶ τελειωσάντων τὰς ἡμέρας, ἐν τῷ ὑποστρέφειν αὐτοὺς ὑπέμεινεν Ἰησοῦς ὁ παῖς ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ, καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ.
Thinking he was in their group of travelers, they went a day's journey. Then they began looking for him among their relatives and friends.
νομίσαντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐν τῇ συνοδίᾳ ἦλθον ἡμέρας ὁδὸν καὶ ἀνεζήτουν αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γνωστοῖς,
When they did not find him, they went back to Jerusalem to search for him.
καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἀναζητοῦντες αὐτόν.
After three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ ἡμέρας τρεῖς εὗρον αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καθεζόμενον ἐν μέσῳ τῶν διδασκάλων καὶ ἀκούοντα αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπερωτῶντα αὐτούς·
Everyone who heard him was astonished at his understanding and his answers.
ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῇ συνέσει καὶ ταῖς ἀποκρίσεσιν αὐτοῦ.
When his parents saw him, they were overwhelmed, and his mother said to him, "Son,[^31] why have you treated us like this? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in great distress."
καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐξεπλάγησαν, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ· Τέκνον, τί ἐποίησας ἡμῖν οὕτως; ἰδοὺ ὁ πατήρ σου καὶ ἐγὼ ὀδυνώμενοι ἐζητοῦμέν σε.
He said to them, "Why were you searching for me? Didn't you know that I had to be in my Father's house?"[^32]
καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί ὅτι ἐζητεῖτέ με; οὐκ ᾔδειτε ὅτι ἐν τοῖς τοῦ πατρός μου δεῖ εἶναί με;
But they did not understand what he was saying to them.
καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐ συνῆκαν τὸ ῥῆμα ὃ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς.
Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and he was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
καὶ κατέβη μετʼ αὐτῶν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς Ναζαρέθ, καὶ ἦν ὑποτασσόμενος αὐτοῖς. καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ διετήρει πάντα τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς.
And Jesus grew in wisdom and stature,[^33] and in favor with God and people.
Καὶ Ἰησοῦς προέκοπτεν σοφίᾳ καὶ ἡλικίᾳ καὶ χάριτι παρὰ θεῷ καὶ ἀνθρώποις.

n.1: Augustus was the first Roman emperor, ruling from 27 BC to AD 14.
n.2: Greek *oikoumene*, "the inhabited world", meaning the Roman Empire. *Registered*: listed in a census.
n.3: Quirinius was governor of Syria from AD 6, when he carried out a census of Judea recorded by the historian Josephus (*Antiquities* 18.1–2). Luke places the birth of Jesus in the reign of Herod the Great (1:5), who died in 4 BC. How Luke's dating relates to these dates is debated. Some take the Greek to mean "This registration took place before Quirinius was governor of Syria."
n.4: David's hometown (1 Samuel 17:12).
n.5: Many manuscripts read "Mary, his engaged wife".
n.6: Literally "swaddled him", wrapping a newborn baby tightly in bands of cloth; also in verse 12.
n.7: A feeding trough for animals; also in verses 12 and 16.
n.8: Or "the inn". Greek *katalyma*, a place to stay; in 22:11 it is the guest room of a house.
n.9: Literally "they feared a great fear".
n.10: Greek *christos kyrios*, "Messiah and Lord", or "the Lord Messiah"; traditionally "Christ the Lord".
n.11: Traditionally "the heavenly host", the angels as God's army.
n.12: Literally "among people of good pleasure", that is, people on whom God's favor rests. Many manuscripts read "and on earth peace, goodwill among people". In Greek the difference is a single letter (*eudokias*, *eudokia*).
n.13: The Law of Moses set a time of purification for a mother after childbirth (Leviticus 12:1–8). The Greek says "their purification".
n.14: Exodus 13:2, 12. In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, Yahweh.
n.15: Leviticus 12:8, the offering of a mother who could not afford a lamb.
n.16: That is, the time when God would comfort his people (Isaiah 40:1; 49:13).
n.19: Or "releasing your slave", that is, letting him die. The words *Master* (Greek *despotes*) and *servant* (*doulos*) are those used of an owner and a slave. The song (verses 29–32) is known as the Nunc Dimittis, from its first words in Latin.
n.22: Many manuscripts read "Joseph and his mother were amazed".
n.23: Literally "is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign spoken against".
n.25: Or "she had been a widow for eighty-four years".
n.30: Many manuscripts read "Joseph and his mother did not know it".
n.32: Or "about my Father's business". Literally "in the things of my Father".
n.33: Or "in years". Greek *helikia* means both age and height.

v: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar,[^1] when Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea,[^2] Herod was tetrarch[^3] of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,

Ἐν ἔτει δὲ πεντεκαιδεκάτῳ τῆς ἡγεμονίας Τιβερίου Καίσαρος, ἡγεμονεύοντος Ποντίου Πιλάτου τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ τετρααρχοῦντος τῆς Γαλιλαίας Ἡρῴδου, Φιλίππου δὲ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ τετρααρχοῦντος τῆς Ἰτουραίας καὶ Τραχωνίτιδος χώρας, καὶ Λυσανίου τῆς Ἀβιληνῆς τετρααρχοῦντος,
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas,[^4] the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
ἐπὶ ἀρχιερέως Ἅννα καὶ Καϊάφα, ἐγένετο ῥῆμα θεοῦ ἐπὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν Ζαχαρίου υἱὸν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ.
He went into all the region around the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance[^5] for the forgiveness of sins,
καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς πᾶσαν περίχωρον τοῦ Ἰορδάνου κηρύσσων βάπτισμα μετανοίας εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν,
as it is written in the book of the words of the prophet Isaiah: "A voice is shouting in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way for the Lord; make his paths straight.
ὡς γέγραπται ἐν βίβλῳ λόγων Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου· Φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill made low. The crooked ways will become straight, and the rough places smooth roads,
πᾶσα φάραγξ πληρωθήσεται καὶ πᾶν ὄρος καὶ βουνὸς ταπεινωθήσεται, καὶ ἔσται τὰ σκολιὰ εἰς εὐθείαν καὶ αἱ τραχεῖαι εἰς ὁδοὺς λείας·
and all people[^6] will see the salvation of God.'"[^7]
καὶ ὄψεται πᾶσα σὰρξ τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ θεοῦ.
So John said to the crowds who came out to be baptized by him, "You brood of vipers![^8] Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
Ἔλεγεν οὖν τοῖς ἐκπορευομένοις ὄχλοις βαπτισθῆναι ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ· Γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, τίς ὑπέδειξεν ὑμῖν φυγεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς μελλούσης ὀργῆς;
Produce fruit, then, that fits your repentance,[^9] and don't begin to say to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' For I tell you, God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
ποιήσατε οὖν καρποὺς ἀξίους τῆς μετανοίας· καὶ μὴ ἄρξησθε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ, λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι δύναται ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν λίθων τούτων ἐγεῖραι τέκνα τῷ Ἀβραάμ.
Even now the ax is lying at the root of the trees. So every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire."
ἤδη δὲ καὶ ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται· πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
The crowds asked him, "What then should we do?"
Καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι λέγοντες· Τί οὖν ποιήσωμεν;
He answered them, "Whoever has two tunics should share with the one who has none, and whoever has food should do the same."
ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁ ἔχων δύο χιτῶνας μεταδότω τῷ μὴ ἔχοντι, καὶ ὁ ἔχων βρώματα ὁμοίως ποιείτω.
Tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, "Teacher, what should we do?"
ἦλθον δὲ καὶ τελῶναι βαπτισθῆναι καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε, τί ποιήσωμεν;
He told them, "Collect no more than you have been ordered to."
ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μηδὲν πλέον παρὰ τὸ διατεταγμένον ὑμῖν πράσσετε.
Soldiers also asked him, "And what should we do?" He told them, "Don't take money from anyone by force or by false accusation, and be content with your wages."
ἐπηρώτων δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ στρατευόμενοι λέγοντες· Τί ποιήσωμεν καὶ ἡμεῖς; καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Μηδένα διασείσητε μηδὲ συκοφαντήσητε, καὶ ἀρκεῖσθε τοῖς ὀψωνίοις ὑμῶν.
The people were waiting expectantly, and all of them were wondering in their hearts about John, whether he might be the Messiah.
Προσδοκῶντος δὲ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ διαλογιζομένων πάντων ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν περὶ τοῦ Ἰωάννου, μήποτε αὐτὸς εἴη ὁ χριστός,
John answered them all, "I baptize you with water, but someone more powerful than I am is coming. I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
ἀπεκρίνατο λέγων πᾶσιν ὁ Ἰωάννης· Ἐγὼ μὲν ὕδατι βαπτίζω ὑμᾶς· ἔρχεται δὲ ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς λῦσαι τὸν ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων αὐτοῦ· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί·
His winnowing fork[^10] is in his hand, to clear his threshing floor and to gather the wheat into his barn, but he will burn up the chaff with fire that never goes out."
οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ διακαθᾶραι τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ συναγαγεῖν τὸν σῖτον εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην αὐτοῦ, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ.
So with many other appeals he proclaimed the good news to the people.
Πολλὰ μὲν οὖν καὶ ἕτερα παρακαλῶν εὐηγγελίζετο τὸν λαόν·
But Herod the tetrarch had been rebuked by John because of Herodias, his brother's wife, and because of all the evil things Herod had done.
ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης, ἐλεγχόμενος ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ περὶ Ἡρῳδιάδος τῆς γυναικὸς τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν πονηρῶν ὁ Ἡρῴδης,
He added this to them all: he locked John up in prison.
προσέθηκεν καὶ τοῦτο ἐπὶ πᾶσιν, καὶ κατέκλεισεν τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐν φυλακῇ.
When all the people were being baptized, Jesus also was baptized. And while he was praying, heaven was opened,
Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ βαπτισθῆναι ἅπαντα τὸν λαὸν καὶ Ἰησοῦ βαπτισθέντος καὶ προσευχομένου ἀνεῳχθῆναι τὸν οὐρανὸν
and the Holy Spirit came down on him in bodily form like a dove. And a voice came from heaven: "You are my Son, whom I love. I am delighted with you."[^11]
καὶ καταβῆναι τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον σωματικῷ εἴδει ὡς περιστερὰν ἐπʼ αὐτόν, καὶ φωνὴν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ γενέσθαι· Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν σοὶ εὐδόκησα.
Jesus was about thirty years old when he began his work.[^12] He was the son, as people supposed,[^13] of Joseph, the son of Heli,[^14]
Καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἀρχόμενος ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα, ὢν υἱός, ὡς ἐνομίζετο, Ἰωσὴφ τοῦ Ἠλὶ
the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
τοῦ Μαθθὰτ τοῦ Λευὶ τοῦ Μελχὶ τοῦ Ἰανναὶ τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ
the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
τοῦ Ματταθίου τοῦ Ἀμὼς τοῦ Ναοὺμ τοῦ Ἑσλὶ τοῦ Ναγγαὶ
the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Josech,[^15] the son of Joda,
τοῦ Μάαθ τοῦ Ματταθίου τοῦ Σεμεῒν τοῦ Ἰωσὴχ τοῦ Ἰωδὰ
the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel,[^16] the son of Neri,
τοῦ Ἰωανὰν τοῦ Ῥησὰ τοῦ Ζοροβαβὲλ τοῦ Σαλαθιὴλ τοῦ Νηρὶ
the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmadam, the son of Er,
τοῦ Μελχὶ τοῦ Ἀδδὶ τοῦ Κωσὰμ τοῦ Ἐλμαδὰμ τοῦ Ἢρ
the son of Joshua,[^17] the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
τοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ἐλιέζερ τοῦ Ἰωρὶμ τοῦ Μαθθὰτ τοῦ Λευὶ
the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliakim,
τοῦ Συμεὼν τοῦ Ἰούδα τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ τοῦ Ἰωνὰμ τοῦ Ἐλιακὶμ
the son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan,[^18] the son of David,
τοῦ Μελεὰ τοῦ Μεννὰ τοῦ Ματταθὰ τοῦ Ναθὰμ τοῦ Δαυὶδ
the son of Jesse, the son of Obed,[^19] the son of Boaz, the son of Sala,[^20] the son of Nahshon,
τοῦ Ἰεσσαὶ τοῦ Ἰωβὴλ τοῦ Βόος τοῦ Σαλὰ τοῦ Ναασσὼν
the son of Amminadab, the son of Admin, the son of Arni,[^21] the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
τοῦ Ἀμιναδὰβ τοῦ Ἀδμὶν τοῦ Ἀρνὶ τοῦ Ἑσρὼμ τοῦ Φαρὲς τοῦ Ἰούδα
the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
τοῦ Ἰακὼβ τοῦ Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ τοῦ Θάρα τοῦ Ναχὼρ
the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
τοῦ Σεροὺχ τοῦ Ῥαγαὺ τοῦ Φάλεκ τοῦ Ἔβερ τοῦ Σαλὰ
the son of Cainan,[^22] the son of Arpachshad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
τοῦ Καϊνὰμ τοῦ Ἀρφαξὰδ τοῦ Σὴμ τοῦ Νῶε τοῦ Λάμεχ
the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Kenan,[^23]
τοῦ Μαθουσαλὰ τοῦ Ἑνὼχ τοῦ Ἰάρετ τοῦ Μαλελεὴλ τοῦ Καϊνὰμ
the son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
τοῦ Ἐνὼς τοῦ Σὴθ τοῦ Ἀδὰμ τοῦ θεοῦ.

n.1: Tiberius became emperor in AD 14, so his fifteenth year was about AD 28.
n.2: Pilate was the Roman prefect of Judea from AD 26 to 36.
n.3: Literally "ruler of a fourth", a title for a ruler of part of a kingdom under Roman control. This Herod is Herod Antipas, a son of Herod the Great, who ruled Galilee and Perea from 4 BC to AD 39. Philip was another son of Herod the Great.
n.4: Literally "in the time of the high priest Annas and Caiaphas". Annas was high priest from AD 6 to 15, and his son-in-law Caiaphas from about AD 18 to 36 (John 18:13). Annas kept great influence and is still called high priest in Acts 4:6.
n.5: A baptism expressing a change of heart and life. Greek *metanoia*, a turning around of mind and life.
n.6: Literally "all flesh".
n.7: Isaiah 40:3–5, following the Greek translation. In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, Yahweh. Where verse 6 has "and all people will see the salvation of God", the Hebrew reads "Then the glory of Yahweh will be revealed, and all people will see it together."
n.8: Literally "offspring of vipers".
n.9: Literally "fruits worthy of repentance".
n.10: A wooden fork for tossing threshed grain into the air, so that the wind would blow the chaff away.
n.11: Or "You are my beloved Son; I take great pleasure in you." Compare Psalm 2:7; Isaiah 42:1.
n.12: Literally "Jesus himself was beginning, about thirty years old".
n.13: Literally "as was thought".
n.14: In verses 23–38 the Greek says only "of Heli, of Matthat …"; "the son" is understood. Names found in the Old Testament are spelled here as in this translation's Old Testament, though Luke gives them in Greek forms, for example *Phares* for Perez and *Ragau* for Reu.
n.16: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel led the return from exile (Ezra 3:2; Haggai 1:1). In 1 Chronicles 3:17–19 Shealtiel is a son of King Jeconiah, as in Matthew 1:12, and Zerubbabel is a son of Shealtiel's brother Pedaiah. Here Shealtiel's father is Neri.
n.17: Greek *Iesous*, the same name as Jesus; Joshua is its Hebrew form. Many manuscripts read "Jose".
n.18: Nathan was a son of David born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:14; 1 Chronicles 3:5). From David to Joseph, Luke traces the line through Nathan, while Matthew 1:6–16 traces it through Solomon and the kings of Judah. The two lists meet only at Shealtiel and Zerubbabel, and they name different fathers for Joseph: Heli here, Jacob in Matthew 1:16.
n.19: The SBLGNT spells the name *Iobel*; in Matthew 1:5 it is *Iobed*.
n.20: Called Salmah and Salmon in Ruth 4:20–21, and Salma in 1 Chronicles 2:11. Many manuscripts read "Salmon".
n.21: Ruth 4:19 and 1 Chronicles 2:9–10 have only Ram between Hezron and Amminadab. Many manuscripts read "the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram" (a Greek form of Ram), and some leave out Amminadab: "the son of Admin, the son of Arni".
n.22: Cainan is not in the Hebrew text of Genesis 11:12 or 1 Chronicles 1:18, 24, where Arpachshad is the father of Shelah. The Septuagint includes him (Genesis 10:24; 11:12–13).
n.23: Greek *Kainam*, the same form as in verse 36.

v: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit in the wilderness
Ἰησοῦς δὲ πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου ὑπέστρεψεν ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ ἤγετο ἐν τῷ πνεύματι ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ
for forty days, being tested[^1] by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and when they were over, he was hungry.
ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου. καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις, καὶ συντελεσθεισῶν αὐτῶν ἐπείνασεν.
The devil said to him, "If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread."
εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ διάβολος· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰπὲ τῷ λίθῳ τούτῳ ἵνα γένηται ἄρτος.
Jesus answered him, "It is written: 'People do not live on bread alone.'"[^2]
καὶ ἀπεκρίθη πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Γέγραπται ὅτι Οὐκ ἐπʼ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος.
Then he led him up and in an instant showed him all the kingdoms of the world.[^3]
Καὶ ἀναγαγὼν αὐτὸν ἔδειξεν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐν στιγμῇ χρόνου·
The devil said to him, "I will give you all this authority and their glory, for it has been handed over to me, and I give it to anyone I wish.
καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ διάβολος· Σοὶ δώσω τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἅπασαν καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν, ὅτι ἐμοὶ παραδέδοται καὶ ᾧ ἂν θέλω δίδωμι αὐτήν·
So if you worship me,[^4] it will all be yours."
σὺ οὖν ἐὰν προσκυνήσῃς ἐνώπιον ἐμοῦ, ἔσται σοῦ πᾶσα.
Jesus answered him,[^5] "It is written: 'Worship the Lord your God, and serve him only.'"[^6]
καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Γέγραπται· Κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις.
Then he brought him to Jerusalem, set him on the highest point[^7] of the temple, and said to him, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here.
Ἤγαγεν δὲ αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ ἔστησεν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, βάλε σεαυτὸν ἐντεῦθεν κάτω·
For it is written: 'He will command his angels concerning you, to guard you,'
γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ τοῦ διαφυλάξαι σε,
and, 'They will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.'"[^8]
καὶ ὅτι Ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε μήποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου.
Jesus answered him, "It is said: 'Do not put the Lord your God to the test.'"[^9]
καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Εἴρηται· Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου.
When the devil had finished every test, he left him until an opportune time.
καὶ συντελέσας πάντα πειρασμὸν ὁ διάβολος ἀπέστη ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι καιροῦ.
Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and news about him spread through the whole surrounding region.
Καὶ ὑπέστρεψεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ πνεύματος εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν. καὶ φήμη ἐξῆλθεν καθʼ ὅλης τῆς περιχώρου περὶ αὐτοῦ.
He taught in their synagogues, and everyone praised him.
καὶ αὐτὸς ἐδίδασκεν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν, δοξαζόμενος ὑπὸ πάντων.
He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and on the Sabbath day he went into the synagogue, as was his custom. He stood up to read,
Καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς Ναζαρά, οὗ ἦν τεθραμμένος, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν κατὰ τὸ εἰωθὸς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν, καὶ ἀνέστη ἀναγνῶναι.
and the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He unrolled the scroll and found the place where it was written:
καὶ ἐπεδόθη αὐτῷ βιβλίον τοῦ προφήτου Ἠσαΐου καὶ ἀναπτύξας τὸ βιβλίον εὗρεν τὸν τόπον οὗ ἦν γεγραμμένον·

"The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me[^10] to proclaim freedom for the captives and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free,
Πνεῦμα κυρίου ἐπʼ ἐμέ, οὗ εἵνεκεν ἔχρισέν με εὐαγγελίσασθαι πτωχοῖς, ἀπέσταλκέν με κηρύξαι αἰχμαλώτοις ἄφεσιν καὶ τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν, ἀποστεῖλαι τεθραυσμένους ἐν ἀφέσει,
to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor."[^11]
κηρύξαι ἐνιαυτὸν κυρίου δεκτόν.
Then he rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on him.
καὶ πτύξας τὸ βιβλίον ἀποδοὺς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ ἐκάθισεν· καὶ πάντων οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἦσαν ἀτενίζοντες αὐτῷ.
He began by saying to them, "Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing."
ἤρξατο δὲ λέγειν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Σήμερον πεπλήρωται ἡ γραφὴ αὕτη ἐν τοῖς ὠσὶν ὑμῶν.
Everyone spoke well of him[^12] and was amazed at the gracious words that came from his mouth. They said, "Isn't this Joseph's son?"
καὶ πάντες ἐμαρτύρουν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις τῆς χάριτος τοῖς ἐκπορευομένοις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον· Οὐχὶ υἱός ἐστιν Ἰωσὴφ οὗτος;
He said to them, "No doubt you will quote this proverb to me: 'Doctor, heal yourself! Do here in your hometown the things we have heard you did in Capernaum.'"
καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Πάντως ἐρεῖτέ μοι τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην· Ἰατρέ, θεράπευσον σεαυτόν· ὅσα ἠκούσαμεν γενόμενα εἰς τὴν Καφαρναοὺμ ποίησον καὶ ὧδε ἐν τῇ πατρίδι σου.
He went on, "Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted[^13] in his hometown.
εἶπεν δέ· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς προφήτης δεκτός ἐστιν ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ.
But I tell you the truth: there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three years and six months and a great famine came over the whole land.[^14]
ἐπʼ ἀληθείας δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, πολλαὶ χῆραι ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἠλίου ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ, ὅτε ἐκλείσθη ὁ οὐρανὸς ἐπὶ ἔτη τρία καὶ μῆνας ἕξ, ὡς ἐγένετο λιμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν,
Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but only to a widow at Zarephath in the region of Sidon.
καὶ πρὸς οὐδεμίαν αὐτῶν ἐπέμφθη Ἠλίας εἰ μὴ εἰς Σάρεπτα τῆς Σιδωνίας πρὸς γυναῖκα χήραν.
And there were many in Israel with skin diseases[^15] in the time of the prophet Elisha, yet none of them was made clean except Naaman the Syrian."[^16]
καὶ πολλοὶ λεπροὶ ἦσαν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ ἐπὶ Ἐλισαίου τοῦ προφήτου, καὶ οὐδεὶς αὐτῶν ἐκαθαρίσθη, εἰ μὴ Ναιμὰν ὁ Σύρος.
When they heard this, everyone in the synagogue was filled with rage.
καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν πάντες θυμοῦ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἀκούοντες ταῦτα,
They got up, drove him out of the town, and led him to the brow of the hill on which their town was built, in order to throw him down the cliff.
καὶ ἀναστάντες ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἕως ὀφρύος τοῦ ὄρους ἐφʼ οὗ ἡ πόλις ᾠκοδόμητο αὐτῶν, ὥστε κατακρημνίσαι αὐτόν·
But he passed through the middle of them and went on his way.
αὐτὸς δὲ διελθὼν διὰ μέσου αὐτῶν ἐπορεύετο.
He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and on the Sabbath he was teaching them.
Καὶ κατῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας. καὶ ἦν διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν·
They were amazed at his teaching, because his word had authority.
καὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐν ἐξουσίᾳ ἦν ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ.
In the synagogue there was a man who had the spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a loud voice,
καὶ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἔχων πνεῦμα δαιμονίου ἀκαθάρτου, καὶ ἀνέκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ·
"Ha![^17] What do you want with us,[^18] Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God!"
Ἔα, τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Ναζαρηνέ; ἦλθες ἀπολέσαι ἡμᾶς; οἶδά σε τίς εἶ, ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ.
Jesus rebuked him: "Be quiet, and come out of him!" The demon threw the man down in front of them all and came out of him without doing him any harm.
καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Φιμώθητι καὶ ἔξελθε ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ. καὶ ῥίψαν αὐτὸν τὸ δαιμόνιον εἰς τὸ μέσον ἐξῆλθεν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ μηδὲν βλάψαν αὐτόν.
Everyone was amazed, and they said to one another, "What is this word?[^19] With authority and power he gives orders to the unclean spirits, and they come out!"
καὶ ἐγένετο θάμβος ἐπὶ πάντας, καὶ συνελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες· Τίς ὁ λόγος οὗτος ὅτι ἐν ἐξουσίᾳ καὶ δυνάμει ἐπιτάσσει τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις πνεύμασιν, καὶ ἐξέρχονται;
And news about him spread to every place in the surrounding region.
καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο ἦχος περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς πάντα τόπον τῆς περιχώρου.
Jesus left the synagogue and went into Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and they asked him to help her.[^20]
Ἀναστὰς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς συναγωγῆς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Σίμωνος. πενθερὰ δὲ τοῦ Σίμωνος ἦν συνεχομένη πυρετῷ μεγάλῳ, καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν περὶ αὐτῆς.
He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. At once she got up and began to serve them.
καὶ ἐπιστὰς ἐπάνω αὐτῆς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ πυρετῷ, καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτήν· παραχρῆμα δὲ ἀναστᾶσα διηκόνει αὐτοῖς.
As the sun was setting, all who had people sick with various diseases brought them to him. He laid his hands on each one of them and healed them.
Δύνοντος δὲ τοῦ ἡλίου ἅπαντες ὅσοι εἶχον ἀσθενοῦντας νόσοις ποικίλαις ἤγαγον αὐτοὺς πρὸς αὐτόν· ὁ δὲ ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ αὐτῶν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπιτιθεὶς ἐθεράπευεν αὐτούς.
Demons also came out of many people, shouting, "You are the Son of God!"[^21] But he rebuked them and would not let them speak, because they knew he was the Messiah.
ἐξήρχετο δὲ καὶ δαιμόνια ἀπὸ πολλῶν κραυγάζοντα καὶ λέγοντα ὅτι Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ ἐπιτιμῶν οὐκ εἴα αὐτὰ λαλεῖν, ὅτι ᾔδεισαν τὸν χριστὸν αὐτὸν εἶναι.
At daybreak Jesus left and went to a deserted place. The crowds were looking for him, and when they came to him, they tried to keep him from leaving them.
Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἔρημον τόπον· καὶ οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπεζήτουν αὐτόν, καὶ ἦλθον ἕως αὐτοῦ, καὶ κατεῖχον αὐτὸν τοῦ μὴ πορεύεσθαι ἀπʼ αὐτῶν.
But he said to them, "I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns too, because that is why I was sent."
ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Καὶ ταῖς ἑτέραις πόλεσιν εὐαγγελίσασθαί με δεῖ τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅτι ἐπὶ τοῦτο ἀπεστάλην.
So he kept proclaiming the message in the synagogues of Judea.[^22]
καὶ ἦν κηρύσσων εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς τῆς Ἰουδαίας.

n.1: Or "tempted". The Greek word means both; also in verse 13.
n.2: Deuteronomy 8:3. Many manuscripts add "but on every word of God".
n.3: Many manuscripts read "Then the devil led him up on a high mountain and in an instant showed him all the kingdoms of the world."
n.4: Literally "worship before me".
n.5: Many manuscripts add "Get behind me, Satan!"
n.6: Deuteronomy 6:13. In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, Yahweh. The Hebrew reads "Fear" where Luke has "Worship", and does not have "only".
n.7: Literally "the little wing", perhaps a corner of the temple walls high above the valley.
n.8: Psalm 91:11–12, leaving out "in all your ways".
n.9: Deuteronomy 6:16. In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, Yahweh.
n.10: Many manuscripts add "to heal the brokenhearted".
n.11: Isaiah 61:1–2, mostly following the Greek translation, with "to set the oppressed free" from 58:6. In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, Yahweh. The Hebrew also has "to bind up the brokenhearted" after "He has sent me", and where Luke has "recovery of sight for the blind", it has "release for the prisoners". The reading stops before Isaiah's next words, "and the day of vengeance of our God".
n.12: Or "testified about him".
n.13: Greek *dektos*, the word translated "favor" in verse 19.
n.15: Greek *lepros*, traditionally "leper". The word covered various skin diseases, not only what is now called leprosy.
n.17: Greek *ea*, a cry of surprise or displeasure. Or "Leave us alone!"
n.18: Literally "What to us and to you?", an idiom: "What do we have to do with you?"
n.19: Or "What kind of message is this?"
n.21: Many manuscripts read "You are the Messiah, the Son of God!"
n.22: Luke sometimes uses "Judea" for the whole land of the Jews (1:5; 7:17; 23:5). Many manuscripts read "Galilee".

v: Once, as the crowd was pressing around Jesus to hear the word of God, he was standing beside the Lake of Gennesaret.[^1]
Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν ὄχλον ἐπικεῖσθαι αὐτῷ καὶ ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἑστὼς παρὰ τὴν λίμνην Γεννησαρέτ,
He saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had got out of them and were washing their nets.
καὶ εἶδεν δύο πλοῖα ἑστῶτα παρὰ τὴν λίμνην, οἱ δὲ ἁλιεῖς ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ἀποβάντες ἔπλυνον τὰ δίκτυα.
He got into one of the boats, the one that belonged to Simon, and asked him to put out a little way from the shore. Then he sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.
ἐμβὰς δὲ εἰς ἓν τῶν πλοίων, ὃ ἦν Σίμωνος, ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἐπαναγαγεῖν ὀλίγον, καθίσας δὲ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ἐδίδασκεν τοὺς ὄχλους.
When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, "Put out into the deep water, and let down your nets for a catch."
ὡς δὲ ἐπαύσατο λαλῶν, εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα· Ἐπανάγαγε εἰς τὸ βάθος καὶ χαλάσατε τὰ δίκτυα ὑμῶν εἰς ἄγραν.
Simon answered, "Master,[^2] we worked hard all night and caught nothing. But because you say so,[^3] I will let down the nets."
καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν· Ἐπιστάτα, διʼ ὅλης νυκτὸς κοπιάσαντες οὐδὲν ἐλάβομεν, ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ ῥήματί σου χαλάσω τὰ δίκτυα.
When they had done this, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.
καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντες συνέκλεισαν πλῆθος ἰχθύων πολύ, διερρήσσετο δὲ τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν.
So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. They came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
καὶ κατένευσαν τοῖς μετόχοις ἐν τῷ ἑτέρῳ πλοίῳ τοῦ ἐλθόντας συλλαβέσθαι αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἦλθον, καὶ ἔπλησαν ἀμφότερα τὰ πλοῖα ὥστε βυθίζεσθαι αὐτά.
When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus' knees and said, "Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man!"
ἰδὼν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος προσέπεσεν τοῖς γόνασιν Ἰησοῦ λέγων· Ἔξελθε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι, κύριε·
For he and all who were with him were amazed at the catch of fish they had taken,
θάμβος γὰρ περιέσχεν αὐτὸν καὶ πάντας τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἄγρᾳ τῶν ἰχθύων ὧν συνέλαβον,
and so were James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon's partners. Jesus said to Simon, "Don't be afraid. From now on you will be catching people."[^4]
ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου, οἳ ἦσαν κοινωνοὶ τῷ Σίμωνι. καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ φοβοῦ· ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀνθρώπους ἔσῃ ζωγρῶν.
So when they had brought their boats to shore, they left everything and followed him.
καὶ καταγαγόντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἀφέντες πάντα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man covered with a skin disease[^5] was there. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face and begged him, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν μιᾷ τῶν πόλεων καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ πλήρης λέπρας· καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐδεήθη αὐτοῦ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.
Jesus reached out his hand and touched him. "I am willing," he said. "Be made clean!" At once the skin disease left him.
καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ εἰπών· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι· καὶ εὐθέως ἡ λέπρα ἀπῆλθεν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
Jesus ordered him to tell no one. "But go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as evidence for them."[^6]
καὶ αὐτὸς παρήγγειλεν αὐτῷ μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν δεῖξον σεαυτὸν τῷ ἱερεῖ, καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου καθὼς προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
But the news about him spread all the more, and large crowds gathered to hear him and to be healed of their diseases.
διήρχετο δὲ μᾶλλον ὁ λόγος περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ συνήρχοντο ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀκούειν καὶ θεραπεύεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀσθενειῶν αὐτῶν·
But he would withdraw to deserted places and pray.
αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑποχωρῶν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις καὶ προσευχόμενος.

One day, while he was teaching, Pharisees and teachers of the Law were sitting there. They had come from every village of Galilee and Judea, and from Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was with him to heal.[^7]

Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διδάσκων, καὶ ἦσαν καθήμενοι Φαρισαῖοι καὶ νομοδιδάσκαλοι οἳ ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες ἐκ πάσης κώμης τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· καὶ δύναμις κυρίου ἦν εἰς τὸ ἰᾶσθαι αὐτόν.
Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a stretcher.[^8] They tried to bring him in and lay him before Jesus.
καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες φέροντες ἐπὶ κλίνης ἄνθρωπον ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος, καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν εἰσενεγκεῖν καὶ θεῖναι ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.
When they found no way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and let him down on his stretcher through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, in front of Jesus.
καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ποίας εἰσενέγκωσιν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα διὰ τῶν κεράμων καθῆκαν αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ κλινιδίῳ εἰς τὸ μέσον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said, "Friend,[^9] your sins are forgiven."
καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἄνθρωπε, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου.
The scribes and the Pharisees began to reason among themselves, "Who is this man who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins but God alone?"
καὶ ἤρξαντο διαλογίζεσθαι οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες· Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὃς λαλεῖ βλασφημίας; τίς δύναται ἁμαρτίας ἀφεῖναι εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ θεός;
Jesus knew what they were thinking, and he answered them, "Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
ἐπιγνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;
Which is easier: to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν· Ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου, ἢ εἰπεῖν· Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;
But so that you may know that the Son of Man[^10] has authority on earth to forgive sins"—he said to the paralyzed man—"I tell you, get up, pick up your stretcher, and go home."
ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας— εἶπεν τῷ παραλελυμένῳ· Σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε καὶ ἄρας τὸ κλινίδιόν σου πορεύου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.
At once the man got up in front of them, picked up what he had been lying on, and went home, praising God.
καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀναστὰς ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν, ἄρας ἐφʼ ὃ κατέκειτο, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ δοξάζων τὸν θεόν.
Amazement seized them all, and they praised God. They were filled with awe and said, "We have seen incredible things today."
καὶ ἔκστασις ἔλαβεν ἅπαντας καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεόν, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν φόβου λέγοντες ὅτι Εἴδομεν παράδοξα σήμερον.
After this Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. "Follow me," he said to him.
Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἐθεάσατο τελώνην ὀνόματι Λευὶν καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι.
And Levi left everything, got up, and followed him.
καὶ καταλιπὼν πάντα ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ.
Then Levi held a great banquet for Jesus in his house, and a large crowd of tax collectors and others were at table with them.
Καὶ ἐποίησεν δοχὴν μεγάλην Λευὶς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἦν ὄχλος πολὺς τελωνῶν καὶ ἄλλων οἳ ἦσαν μετʼ αὐτῶν κατακείμενοι.
The Pharisees and their scribes complained to his disciples, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
καὶ ἐγόγγυζον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίετε καὶ πίνετε;
Jesus answered them, "Healthy people don't need a doctor; sick people do.
καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ὑγιαίνοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες·
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance."
οὐκ ἐλήλυθα καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν.
They said to him, "John's disciples often fast and pray, and so do the disciples of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink."[^11]
Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· Οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου νηστεύουσιν πυκνὰ καὶ δεήσεις ποιοῦνται, ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ τῶν Φαρισαίων, οἱ δὲ σοὶ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ πίνουσιν.
He said to them, "Can you make the wedding guests[^12] fast while the bridegroom is with them?
ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μὴ δύνασθε τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετʼ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ποιῆσαι νηστεῦσαι;
But the days will come, and when the bridegroom is taken away from them, then they will fast in those days."
ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι, καὶ ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
He also told them a parable: "No one tears a patch from a new garment and puts it on an old garment. Otherwise he will tear the new garment, and the patch from the new will not match the old.

ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ἀπὸ ἱματίου καινοῦ σχίσας ἐπιβάλλει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν· εἰ δὲ μήγε, καὶ τὸ καινὸν σχίσει καὶ τῷ παλαιῷ οὐ συμφωνήσει τὸ ἐπίβλημα τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ καινοῦ.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise the new wine will burst the skins; it will be spilled, and the skins will be ruined.
καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μήγε, ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος ὁ νέος τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκχυθήσεται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπολοῦνται·
No, new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.[^13]
ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινοὺς βλητέον.
And no one who has drunk old wine wants new, for he says, 'The old is good.'"[^14]
καὶ οὐδεὶς πιὼν παλαιὸν θέλει νέον· λέγει γάρ· Ὁ παλαιὸς χρηστός ἐστιν.

n.1: That is, the Sea of Galilee.
n.2: Greek *epistates*, "master, overseer", a title of respect that only Luke uses for Jesus.
n.3: Literally "at your word".
n.4: Literally "you will be catching people alive".
n.5: Literally "full of *lepra*", traditionally "leprosy". The word covered various skin diseases, not only what is now called leprosy.
n.6: Or "as a testimony against them". The offerings are set out in Leviticus 14:1–32.
n.7: Literally "the power of the Lord was for him to heal". Many manuscripts read "to heal them".
n.8: Greek *kline*, "bed, couch". In verses 19 and 24 Luke uses *klinidion*, "small bed".
n.9: Literally "Man".
n.10: A title Jesus uses for himself in all four Gospels. It recalls "one like a son of man" in Daniel 7:13, and in Hebrew idiom it can also mean simply "a human being".
n.11: Many manuscripts read "Why do John's disciples often fast and pray …?"
n.12: Literally "the sons of the bridechamber".
n.13: Many manuscripts add "and both are preserved".
n.14: Many manuscripts read "no one who has drunk old wine immediately wants new", and "The old is better".

v: One Sabbath[^1] Jesus was going through the grainfields, and his disciples were picking heads of grain, rubbing them in their hands, and eating them.
Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν σαββάτῳ διαπορεύεσθαι αὐτὸν διὰ σπορίμων, καὶ ἔτιλλον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤσθιον τοὺς στάχυας ψώχοντες ταῖς χερσίν.
Some of the Pharisees said, "Why are you doing what is not allowed on the Sabbath?"
τινὲς δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων εἶπαν· Τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν;
Jesus answered them, "Haven't you even read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδὲ τοῦτο ἀνέγνωτε ὃ ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὁπότε ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ὄντες;
He went into the house of God, took the sacred bread,[^2] ate it, and gave some to his companions, though only the priests are allowed to eat it."[^3]
ὡς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως λαβὼν ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔδωκεν τοῖς μετʼ αὐτοῦ, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ μόνους τοὺς ἱερεῖς;
Then he said to them, "The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath."
καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Κύριός ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
On another Sabbath he went into the synagogue and was teaching. A man was there whose right hand was withered.
Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἑτέρῳ σαββάτῳ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν καὶ διδάσκειν· καὶ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ἡ δεξιὰ ἦν ξηρά·
The scribes and the Pharisees were watching him closely to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they could find a reason to accuse him.
παρετηροῦντο δὲ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εἰ ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ θεραπεύει, ἵνα εὕρωσιν κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ.
But he knew their thoughts, and he said to the man with the withered hand, "Get up and stand in the middle." So the man got up and stood there.
αὐτὸς δὲ ᾔδει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν, εἶπεν δὲ τῷ ἀνδρὶ τῷ ξηρὰν ἔχοντι τὴν χεῖρα· Ἔγειρε καὶ στῆθι εἰς τὸ μέσον· καὶ ἀναστὰς ἔστη.
Then Jesus said to them, "I ask you: is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to destroy it?"
εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐπερωτῶ ὑμᾶς, εἰ ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀπολέσαι;
He looked around at them all and said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He did so, and his hand was restored.[^4]
καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντας αὐτοὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρά σου· ὁ δὲ ἐποίησεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ.
But they were filled with fury[^5] and began discussing with one another what they might do to Jesus.
αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐπλήσθησαν ἀνοίας, καὶ διελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους τί ἂν ποιήσαιεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
In those days he went out to the mountain to pray, and he spent the whole night in prayer to God.
Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἐξελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι, καὶ ἦν διανυκτερεύων ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ.
When day came, he called his disciples to him and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles:[^6]
καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡμέρα, προσεφώνησεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκλεξάμενος ἀπʼ αὐτῶν δώδεκα, οὓς καὶ ἀποστόλους ὠνόμασεν,
Simon, whom he also named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;
Σίμωνα ὃν καὶ ὠνόμασεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον
Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon, who was called the Zealot;[^7]
καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν καλούμενον Ζηλωτὴν
Judas son of James,[^8] and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριὼθ ὃς ἐγένετο προδότης.
He came down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of his disciples was there, and a great number of people from all Judea and Jerusalem and from the coast of Tyre and Sidon.
Καὶ καταβὰς μετʼ αὐτῶν ἔστη ἐπὶ τόπου πεδινοῦ, καὶ ὄχλος πολὺς μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, καὶ πλῆθος πολὺ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ τῆς παραλίου Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος,
They had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases, and those who were troubled by unclean spirits were healed.
οἳ ἦλθον ἀκοῦσαι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰαθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν νόσων αὐτῶν· καὶ οἱ ἐνοχλούμενοι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ἐθεραπεύοντο·
The whole crowd was trying to touch him, because power was coming out from him and healing them all.
καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐζήτουν ἅπτεσθαι αὐτοῦ, ὅτι δύναμις παρʼ αὐτοῦ ἐξήρχετο καὶ ἰᾶτο πάντας.
Then he looked up at his disciples and said: "Blessed[^9] are you who are poor, for the kingdom of God is yours.[^10]
Καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν· Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοί, ὅτι ὑμετέρα ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες νῦν, ὅτι χορτασθήσεσθε. μακάριοι οἱ κλαίοντες νῦν, ὅτι γελάσετε.
Blessed are you when people hate you, when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil[^11] because of the Son of Man.
Μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν μισήσωσιν ὑμᾶς οἱ ἄνθρωποι, καὶ ὅταν ἀφορίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὀνειδίσωσιν καὶ ἐκβάλωσιν τὸ ὄνομα ὑμῶν ὡς πονηρὸν ἕνεκα τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
Rejoice on that day and leap for joy, for look, your reward in heaven is great. For that is how their ancestors[^12] treated the prophets.
χάρητε ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ σκιρτήσατε, ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ· κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς προφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.
"But woe to you who are rich,[^13] for you have already received your comfort in full.
πλὴν οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς πλουσίοις, ὅτι ἀπέχετε τὴν παράκλησιν ὑμῶν.
Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, οἱ ἐμπεπλησμένοι νῦν, ὅτι πεινάσετε. οὐαί, οἱ γελῶντες νῦν, ὅτι πενθήσετε καὶ κλαύσετε.
Woe to you when everyone speaks well of you, for that is how their ancestors treated the false prophets.
Οὐαὶ ὅταν καλῶς ὑμᾶς εἴπωσιν πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι, κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς ψευδοπροφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.
"But I tell you who are listening: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
Ἀλλὰ ὑμῖν λέγω τοῖς ἀκούουσιν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν, καλῶς ποιεῖτε τοῖς μισοῦσιν ὑμᾶς,
bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ὑμᾶς, προσεύχεσθε περὶ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς.
If anyone strikes you on the cheek, offer the other one too. If anyone takes your cloak, do not hold back your tunic either.[^14]
τῷ τύπτοντί σε ἐπὶ τὴν σιαγόνα πάρεχε καὶ τὴν ἄλλην, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντός σου τὸ ἱμάτιον καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα μὴ κωλύσῃς.
Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.
παντὶ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ μὴ ἀπαίτει.
Do to others as you want them to do to you.
καὶ καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς ὁμοίως.
"If you love those who love you, what credit[^15] is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.
Καὶ εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; καὶ γὰρ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας αὐτοὺς ἀγαπῶσιν.
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.
καὶ ἐὰν ἀγαθοποιῆτε τοὺς ἀγαθοποιοῦντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν.
And if you lend to those from whom you expect to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, to receive as much in return.
καὶ ἐὰν δανίσητε παρʼ ὧν ἐλπίζετε λαβεῖν, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς δανίζουσιν ἵνα ἀπολάβωσιν τὰ ἴσα.

But love your enemies, do good, and lend, expecting nothing in return.[^16] Then your reward will be great, and you will be children[^17] of the Most High, for he is kind to the ungrateful and the wicked.
πλὴν ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ ἀγαθοποιεῖτε καὶ δανίζετε μηδὲν ἀπελπίζοντες· καὶ ἔσται ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολύς, καὶ ἔσεσθε υἱοὶ Ὑψίστου, ὅτι αὐτὸς χρηστός ἐστιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀχαρίστους καὶ πονηρούς.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
γίνεσθε οἰκτίρμονες καθὼς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν οἰκτίρμων ἐστίν·
"Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.[^18]
Καὶ μὴ κρίνετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ κριθῆτε· καὶ μὴ καταδικάζετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ καταδικασθῆτε. ἀπολύετε, καὶ ἀπολυθήσεσθε·
Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be poured into your lap.[^19] For the measure you use will be used to measure you in return."
δίδοτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· μέτρον καλὸν πεπιεσμένον σεσαλευμένον ὑπερεκχυννόμενον δώσουσιν εἰς τὸν κόλπον ὑμῶν· ᾧ γὰρ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε ἀντιμετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.
He also told them a parable: "Can a blind person guide a blind person? Won't they both fall into a pit?
Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς· Μήτι δύναται τυφλὸς τυφλὸν ὁδηγεῖν; οὐχὶ ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον ἐμπεσοῦνται;
A disciple is not above the teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like their teacher.
οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον, κατηρτισμένος δὲ πᾶς ἔσται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ.
Why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye but do not notice the log in your own eye?
τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ δοκὸν τὴν ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ ὀφθαλμῷ οὐ κατανοεῖς;

How can you say to your brother, 'Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,' when you yourself do not see the log in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.

πῶς δύνασαι λέγειν τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἀδελφέ, ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σου, αὐτὸς τὴν ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ δοκὸν οὐ βλέπων; ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον τὴν δοκὸν ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου ἐκβαλεῖν.
"For no good tree produces bad fruit, and no diseased tree produces good fruit.[^20]
Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν δένδρον καλὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν σαπρόν, οὐδὲ πάλιν δένδρον σαπρὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλόν.
Each tree is known by its own fruit. People do not pick figs from thornbushes, or gather grapes from a bramble bush.
ἕκαστον γὰρ δένδρον ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου καρποῦ γινώσκεται· οὐ γὰρ ἐξ ἀκανθῶν συλλέγουσιν σῦκα, οὐδὲ ἐκ βάτου σταφυλὴν τρυγῶσιν.
The good person brings good things out of the good treasure of the heart, and the evil person brings evil things out of evil.[^21] For the mouth speaks from what fills the heart.
ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ προφέρει τὸ ἀγαθόν, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ προφέρει τὸ πονηρόν· ἐκ γὰρ περισσεύματος καρδίας λαλεῖ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ.
"Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord,' and do not do what I say?
Τί δέ με καλεῖτε· Κύριε κύριε, καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω;
Everyone who comes to me, hears my words, and does them—I will show you what he is like.
πᾶς ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρός με καὶ ἀκούων μου τῶν λόγων καὶ ποιῶν αὐτούς, ὑποδείξω ὑμῖν τίνι ἐστὶν ὅμοιος·
He is like a man building a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock. When a flood came, the river burst against that house but could not shake it, because it had been well built.[^22]

ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομοῦντι οἰκίαν ὃς ἔσκαψεν καὶ ἐβάθυνεν καὶ ἔθηκεν θεμέλιον ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν· πλημμύρης δὲ γενομένης προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμὸς τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν σαλεῦσαι αὐτὴν διὰ τὸ καλῶς οἰκοδομῆσθαι αὐτήν.

But the one who hears and does not do them is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. The river burst against it, and at once it collapsed, and the ruin of that house was great."
ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας καὶ μὴ ποιήσας ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομήσαντι οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν χωρὶς θεμελίου, ᾗ προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμός, καὶ εὐθὺς συνέπεσεν, καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ ῥῆγμα τῆς οἰκίας ἐκείνης μέγα.

n.1: Many manuscripts add a word of uncertain meaning, *deuteroproto*, "second-first", before "Sabbath".
n.2: Literally "the bread of the presentation", the twelve loaves set out before God in the sanctuary (Leviticus 24:5–9).
n.3: 1 Samuel 21:2–7 (21:1–6 in most English Bibles).
n.4: Many manuscripts add "as healthy as the other".
n.5: Or "senseless rage". Greek *anoia*, "folly, madness".
n.6: Greek *apostolos*, "one who is sent", a messenger.
n.7: Mark 3:18 calls him "the Cananaean", from an Aramaic word meaning "zealous".
n.8: Literally "Judas of James", usually taken to mean his son. Mark 3:18 has Thaddaeus at this place in the list.
n.9: Greek *makarioi*, "blessed, happy, fortunate": those whom God favors. Also in verses 21–22.
n.10: Literally "Blessed the poor, for yours is the kingdom of God."
n.11: Literally "throw out your name as evil".
n.12: Literally "their fathers"; also in verse 26.
n.13: Greek *ouai*, a cry of grief and warning, like the prophets' *hoy* ("woe"); also in verses 25–26.
n.14: The cloak was the outer garment; the tunic was worn next to the skin.
n.15: Greek *charis*, "grace, favor, thanks"; also in verses 33–34.
n.18: Literally "Release, and you will be released."
n.19: Literally "they will give into your lap", the fold of a robe above the belt, used as a pocket.
n.20: Greek *sapros*, "rotten, decayed", used here of both the tree and the fruit.
n.21: Many manuscripts read "out of the evil treasure of his heart".
n.22: Many manuscripts read "because it had been founded on the rock".

v: When Jesus had finished saying all these things in the hearing of the people, he went into Capernaum.
Ἐπειδὴ ἐπλήρωσεν πάντα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς τοῦ λαοῦ, εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναούμ.
A centurion[^1] there had a servant[^2] whom he valued highly, and the servant was sick and about to die.
Ἑκατοντάρχου δέ τινος δοῦλος κακῶς ἔχων ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν, ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ ἔντιμος.
When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some elders of the Jews to him, asking him to come and save his servant's life.
ἀκούσας δὲ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν πρεσβυτέρους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐρωτῶν αὐτὸν ὅπως ἐλθὼν διασώσῃ τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ.
When they came to Jesus, they pleaded with him earnestly, "He deserves to have you do this for him,
οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν σπουδαίως λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄξιός ἐστιν ᾧ παρέξῃ τοῦτο,
because he loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us."
ἀγαπᾷ γὰρ τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτὸς ᾠκοδόμησεν ἡμῖν.
So Jesus went with them. When he was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to say to him, "Lord, don't trouble yourself, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof.
ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐπορεύετο σὺν αὐτοῖς. ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκίας ἔπεμψεν φίλους ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης λέγων αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μὴ σκύλλου, οὐ γὰρ ἱκανός εἰμι ἵνα ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην μου εἰσέλθῃς·
That is why I did not even consider myself worthy to come to you. But say the word, and let my servant[^3] be healed.
